in_arabic.name: أبكر
in_arabic.meaning: اسم مشتق من أبكار و معناه السابقون إلى الخيرات
in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم أبكر مشتق من الجذر أ-ب-ك-ر و يعني الشخص الذي يتقدم إلى الخيرات و السعي في الطاعات قبل غيره، و يدل على الاجتهاد و الهمة العالية في الأمور الدينية و الدنيوية.

in_urdu.name: ابکر
in_urdu.meaning: سابق الخیرات، اچھے کاموں میں سب سے پہلے کرنے والا
in_urdu.long_meaning: ابکر نام کی اصلیت عربی زبان سے ہے، جس کا مطلب ہے کہ اچھے کاموں میں سب سے پہلے کرنے والا یا خیرات میں سبقت لینے والا۔ یہ نام اسلامی تقویم اور اچھے کاموں میں پہل کرنے کی علامت ہے۔

in_hindi.name: अबकर
in_hindi.meaning: अच्छे कार्यों में पहले करने वाला, पुण्य कार्यों में अग्रणी
in_hindi.long_meaning: अबकर नाम का अर्थ है अच्छे कार्यों में पहले करने वाला या पुण्य कार्यों में अग्रणी होना। यह नाम धार्मिक और सामाजिक कार्यों में सक्रिय रहने और दूसरों से 앞서ने की प्रेरणा देता है।

in_pashto.name: ابکر
in_pashto.meaning: د خیراتو په کارونو کې لومړی کس، نیکمرغه
in_pashto.long_meaning: ابکر نوم د هغو کسانو لپاره کارول کیږي چې په خیراتو او نیکو کارونو کې لومړی ګام اخلي. دا نوم د هغو کسانو ځانګړتیا څرګندوي چې په ټولنه کې د نیکۍ او پرمختګ لپاره کار کوي.

in_english.name: Abkar
in_english.meaning: One who precedes others in good deeds, pioneer in charitable acts
in_english.long_meaning: The name Abkar is derived from the Arabic root 'a-b-k-r', signifying someone who leads in good deeds, charity, and righteousness. It reflects a person of high moral character, who takes initiative in acts of kindness and is revered for their piety and dedication to Islamic values. Historically, names like Abkar have been used to inspire individuals to embody virtues such as compassion, generosity, and leadership in their communities.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Abkar" holds a significant cultural impact in the Islamic community, reflecting the important values of compassion, kindness, and generosity towards the less fortunate. In Islamic tradition, providing for the needy and the poor is considered an essential duty, not only for individual salvation but also for the betterment of the society as a whole. The name "Abkar," hence, serves as a constant reminder of this duty, inspiring those who bear it to uphold these virtues and strive to make a positive difference in their communities.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name "Abkar" transcends its literal meaning and embodies the manifestation of God's love and compassion towards His creations. As indicated in several Quranic verses, helping the poor and the needy is an act of worship, pleasing Allah. Therefore, bearing this name can be considered a blessing, as it is a reminder of this spiritual connection between helping others and drawing closer to Allah. Furthermore, it can be seen as a spiritual reminder to embody the qualities of mercy, compassion, and selflessness, thereby fostering a deeper understanding and connection to the divine.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Khaldun mentioned the city of Abkar in his book 'Al-Ibar', which was completed in 1402 CE. He described it as a significant urban center in the Maghreb, known for its textile industry and trade links to the Mediterranean.

The name 'Abkar' is believed to have been derived from the Arabic word 'abqar' meaning 'copper'. In the 10th century CE, Ibn Hawqal described a town named 'Abqar' that was renowned for its copper mines and metalworking industry in the Jazira region of present-day Syria.
